title: Encore of Episode 21: Stroke of Genius

sentences.en: So, let's hear Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们来听听《小星星》吧。

sentences.en: As amazing as it sounds, I probably can't play that.
sentences.zh: 听起来很神奇，但我可能弹不了那首曲子。

sentences.en: And I can explain why as we start chatting about it.
sentences.zh: 在我们聊起这个话题时，我会解释原因。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: A savant is defined as someone who does not have normal intelligence,
sentences.zh: 学者症候群（Savant）的定义是：一个人虽然智力发育不正常，

sentences.en: but possesses unusual mental abilities.
sentences.zh: 但却拥有非凡的心理能力。

sentences.en: My name is Derek Amato.
sentences.zh: 我叫德里克·阿马托（Derek Amato）。

sentences.en: I am 49 years old.
sentences.zh: 我今年49岁。

sentences.en: I currently live in Virginia.
sentences.zh: 目前住在弗吉尼亚州。

sentences.en: But Derek is an unusual case.
sentences.zh: 但德里克是一个特殊的案例。

sentences.en: He's said to have something called a quiet savant syndrome.
sentences.zh: 据说他患有一种所谓的“后天学者症候群”（quiet savant syndrome）。

sentences.en: It's left him with this incredible ability to compose and play piano.
sentences.zh: 这让他拥有了不可思议的钢琴作曲和演奏能力。

sentences.en: We'll talk about what that means, but let's back up a minute.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会讨论这意味着什么，但让我们先回顾一下过去。

sentences.en: I grew up a typical kid.
sentences.zh: 我从小就是一个普通的孩子。

sentences.en: I was an extremely aggressive athlete.
sentences.zh: 我曾是一名极具攻击性的运动员。

sentences.en: So, that was kind of my thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，那算是我的专长。

sentences.en: I was a baseball, football, basketball player.
sentences.zh: 我打棒球、橄榄球、篮球。

sentences.en: You were a jock.
sentences.zh: 你是个运动健将。

sentences.en: I was a jock, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实是。

sentences.en: I had musical interest from very early on.
sentences.zh: 我很早就对音乐产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: My grandmother was an organ player for the church.
sentences.zh: 我祖母是教堂的管风琴手。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I was around it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我从小就接触这些。

sentences.en: I remember Sunday mornings going, sitting next to her on the bench.
sentences.zh: 我记得周日早上，我会坐在她旁边的长凳上。

sentences.en: And even though I didn't understand, you know, what she was doing or how to play the instrument,
sentences.zh: 虽然我不明白她在做什么，也不知道怎么演奏乐器，

sentences.en: I loved to sit with her and sing.
sentences.zh: 但我喜欢坐在她身边唱歌。

sentences.en: And it was just my comfort zone as a child.
sentences.zh: 那是我童年的舒适区。

sentences.en: When I go to church, I get to sit and watch her play the organ and sing.
sentences.zh: 去教堂时，我能坐着看她弹管风琴、唱歌。

sentences.en: At his mother's insistence, Derek dabbled in music.
sentences.zh: 在母亲的坚持下，德里克曾浅尝辄止地接触过音乐。

sentences.en: He joined the school band, played drums, tinkered around with a guitar, formed a rock band with friends.
sentences.zh: 他参加过学校乐队，打过鼓，摆弄过吉他，还和朋友组建过摇滚乐队。

sentences.en: But he did not take formal lessons or get any musical training.
sentences.zh: 但他从未接受过正规课程或任何音乐训练。

sentences.en: Okay, so that's the setup.
sentences.zh: 好了，背景就是这样。

sentences.en: What happens to Derek in 2006 is both terrifying and fascinating.
sentences.zh: 2006年发生在德里克身上的事，既可怕又迷人。

sentences.en: He was in South Dakota visiting friends and family.
sentences.zh: 当时他在南达科他州探亲访友。

sentences.en: I got together with some friends and we were going to have a little barbecue party at the pool, an indoor pool.
sentences.zh: 我和朋友们聚在一起，打算在泳池边举行一个小烧烤派对，那是一个室内泳池。

sentences.en: And we were horsing around and this young man walked in.
sentences.zh: 我们正在打闹时，一个年轻人走了进来。

sentences.en: He must have been about 14, 12, 14.
sentences.zh: 他大概有14岁，12到14岁左右。

sentences.en: And he had this little miniature football with him.
sentences.zh: 他带着一个小橄榄球。

sentences.en: So, of course, we started throwing the football at each other.
sentences.zh: 于是，我们自然就开始互相扔橄榄球玩了。

sentences.en: And I started, I thought I could just run on the side of the pool and then dive over the water and catch the football in the air.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，我可以沿着泳池边跑，然后跳过水面，在空中接住橄榄球。

sentences.en: And the idea was you would catch it and then fall into the pool.
sentences.zh: 原本的设想是接住球后，人会落入泳池里。

sentences.en: Yeah, just catch it in the air and then fall into the water.
sentences.zh: 对，就是在空中接住球，然后掉进水里。

sentences.en: And so I went running on the side of the pool.
sentences.zh: 于是我沿着泳池边跑了起来。

sentences.en: And I remember, I remember running alongside the pool.
sentences.zh: 我记得，我记得当时沿着泳池跑。

sentences.en: I remember even diving in to catch the ball.
sentences.zh: 我还记得自己跳起来去接球。

sentences.en: And I knew I was diving towards a shallow end.
sentences.zh: 而且我知道自己是朝着浅水区跳的。

sentences.en: I was very aware.
sentences.zh: 我非常清醒。

sentences.en: And I miscalculated the depth, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，我误判了深度。

sentences.en: And I hit the upper left side of my face.
sentences.zh: 我的脸部左上方撞到了池底。

sentences.en: And that's all I remember.
sentences.zh: 之后的事我就不记得了。

sentences.en: It was like an explosion.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像爆炸了一样。

sentences.en: And, you know, most of us have had a head trauma when we were a kid or hit our head.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们大多数人在小时候都受过头部创伤或撞到过头。

sentences.en: And it's that sickening feeling you get when it's like, oh, no, I know something.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉很糟糕，你会意识到：噢，不，我知道出事了。

sentences.en: I just did something extremely wrong.
sentences.zh: 我刚才做了一件极其错误的事。

sentences.en: And this isn't right.
sentences.zh: 这不对劲。

sentences.en: And I knew I had hurt myself.
sentences.zh: 我知道我伤到自己了。

sentences.en: Diagnosis was a massive concussion.
sentences.zh: 诊断结果是严重的脑震荡。

sentences.en: And what was the treatment?
sentences.zh: 那治疗方法是什么？

sentences.en: Relax.
sentences.zh: 放松。

sentences.en: Stay quiet.
sentences.zh: 保持安静。

sentences.en: Lay in bed for a few days.
sentences.zh: 卧床休息几天。

sentences.en: I spent the night at the hospital.
sentences.zh: 我在医院住了一晚。

sentences.en: The next morning, they sent me home.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，他们让我回家了。

sentences.en: I went home and I slept.
sentences.zh: 我回家后就睡了。

sentences.en: I slept for five days, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上睡了五天。

sentences.en: And then you get up and do what?
sentences.zh: 那你起床后做了什么？

sentences.en: We're sitting at the table.
sentences.zh: 我们坐在桌边。

sentences.en: And I said, well, I feel pretty darn good.
sentences.zh: 我说，嗯，我感觉好多了。

sentences.en: I know I had an accident and I'm not sure what happened.
sentences.zh: 我知道我出了事故，但不确定发生了什么。

sentences.en: And I said, well, I'm going to pack and I think I can go back to Denver in a couple days.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我要收拾行李，我想过几天就能回丹佛了。

sentences.en: So I called Rick and I said, why don't you come over and get me?
sentences.zh: 于是我给里克打了电话，说，你过来接我好吗？

sentences.en: We'll say goodbyes and I'll be on my way in a couple days.
sentences.zh: 我们道个别，过几天我就出发。

sentences.en: And so we went over to his apartment and we were just hanging out.
sentences.zh: 我们去了他的公寓，就在那儿闲逛。

sentences.en: And he had this tiny keyboard, just this little piece of junk in the corner.
sentences.zh: 他角落里有个小键盘，就是个破烂玩意儿。

sentences.en: And it was just on the stand, dusty, and not sure if it had ever been played.
sentences.zh: 它就放在架子上，落满了灰，不知道有没有人弹过。

sentences.en: And I kept staring at it as we were talking.
sentences.zh: 我们聊天时，我一直盯着它看。

sentences.en: And we were just sitting talking just like this.
sentences.zh: 我们当时就像这样坐着聊天。

sentences.en: And I kept looking at it and looking at it, curious.
sentences.zh: 我一直看着它，看着它，感到好奇。

sentences.en: I was like, not sure why I was drawn to it.
sentences.zh: 我不确定为什么会被它吸引。

sentences.en: And I finally just walked over to it and I thought, I'll just hit a few of these keys.
sentences.zh: 最后我走过去，心想，我就按几个键试试。

sentences.en: I turn it on and see what happens.
sentences.zh: 我打开它，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: I had no clue.
sentences.zh: 我完全没头绪。

sentences.en: And I sat down and my fingers just went crazy.
sentences.zh: 我坐下来，手指就开始疯狂地动了起来。

sentences.en: My fingers were like somebody just, I don't know, Rick said the ghost of Beethoven jumped into my body.
sentences.zh: 我的手指就像被什么附身了一样，我不知道，里克说贝多芬的灵魂跳进了我的身体。

sentences.en: I don't know how else to explain it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道该怎么解释。

sentences.en: I went crazy and just played and played.
sentences.zh: 我疯了似的弹啊弹。

sentences.en: And it wasn't like I was just picking away.
sentences.zh: 那感觉不像是在乱弹。

sentences.en: What did you play?
sentences.zh: 你弹了什么？

sentences.en: I played, I think it was more of the, it had this more of a classical structure to it.
sentences.zh: 我想，那更像是一种古典音乐的结构。

sentences.en: And I sat there and did this for, I don't know, five, six hours without stopping.
sentences.zh: 我就坐在那儿，弹了大概五六个小时，没停过。

sentences.en: And we just, I remember looking at him and there was tears rolling down his face.
sentences.zh: 我记得看着他，眼泪顺着他的脸流了下来。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a Christian kid.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是个基督徒孩子。

sentences.en: He's a pretty emotional guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个情感很丰富的人。

sentences.en: He's a sweet, sweet man.
sentences.zh: 他是个非常可爱的人。

sentences.en: And he just, you know, he didn't know what to think as, because, I mean, I've known him since we were kids.
sentences.zh: 他不知道该想些什么，因为我们从小就认识。

sentences.en: And he'd never seen me play a piano.
sentences.zh: 他从没见过我弹钢琴。

sentences.en: So he's like, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 所以他问，这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: I'm not sure what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我也不确定是怎么回事。

sentences.en: I didn't want to stop playing because I was like, well, what if I stop and then this doesn't happen tomorrow morning?
sentences.zh: 我不想停下来，因为我在想，万一我停了，明天早上这能力就没了怎么办？

sentences.en: I mean, this is kind of cool.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太酷了。

sentences.en: I don't, I mean, it doesn't happen every day.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，这可不是每天都会发生的事。

sentences.en: You just sit down and start playing a piano.
sentences.zh: 你不可能随便坐下来就开始弹钢琴。

sentences.en: And so I think this is kind of different.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这很特别。

sentences.en: Let's, let's just stay here for a while.
sentences.zh: 我们，我们就在这儿多待一会儿吧。

sentences.en: It must've been two o'clock in the morning and I was exhausted.
sentences.zh: 当时一定是凌晨两点，我精疲力竭。

sentences.en: My brain was flying, still was racing.
sentences.zh: 我的大脑还在飞速运转，依然兴奋不已。

sentences.en: And, um, so he took me back to my mother's house.
sentences.zh: 所以他把我送回了我母亲家。

sentences.en: We had to call it a day.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不结束这一天。

sentences.en: I was, you know, beat up and I went to bed.
sentences.zh: 我当时，你知道，浑身酸痛，就去睡觉了。

sentences.en: And the next morning I woke up and I was, I was paranoid.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上醒来时，我感到很偏执。

sentences.en: I was nervous.
sentences.zh: 我很紧张。

sentences.en: I was scared.
sentences.zh: 我很害怕。

sentences.en: I was like, how am I going to tell my mother, the person that knows me best on this planet?
sentences.zh: 我在想，我该怎么告诉我的母亲，这个世界上最了解我的人？

sentences.en: I just hit my head and I'm a little whacked out.
sentences.zh: 我刚撞了头，现在有点神志不清。

sentences.en: How am I going to tell her that I just discovered that I know how to play the piano fairly well to a person that's known me my entire life, 40 years.
sentences.zh: 我该怎么告诉她，我刚发现自己能弹得一手好钢琴？对于一个认识我整整40年的人来说。

sentences.en: So I said, well, I don't know any other way than to take her to a music store.
sentences.zh: 所以我说，除了带她去乐器店，我想不出别的办法。

sentences.en: So I said, we had a cup of coffee and I said, let's run to the music store real quick.
sentences.zh: 于是我们喝了杯咖啡，我说，我们快去趟乐器店吧。

sentences.en: And she said, what do you want to buy?
sentences.zh: 她说，你想买什么？

sentences.en: And I said, nothing.
sentences.zh: 我说，什么都不买。

sentences.en: I said, I just want to show you something real faSt.
sentences.zh: 我说，我只是想很快给你展示点东西。

sentences.en: I wouldn't tell her.
sentences.zh: 我没告诉她。

sentences.en: We get to the music store.
sentences.zh: 我们到了乐器店。

sentences.en: We, we walk in.
sentences.zh: 我们走了进去。

sentences.en: The salesman says, I don't know, like, you know, he can kind of help you.
sentences.zh: 售货员说，我不知道，他可以帮你。

sentences.en: He wants to sell me something.
sentences.zh: 他想卖给我点什么。

sentences.en: And I said, if you show me how to get this piano, this digital piano on, that's all I need.
sentences.zh: 我说，如果你能教我怎么打开这台钢琴，这台数码钢琴，这就够了。

sentences.en: And then give me just 10 minutes.
sentences.zh: 然后给我10分钟就行。

sentences.en: So he turns it on, shows me how to turn the darn thing on.
sentences.zh: 他打开了琴，教我怎么打开这该死的东西。

sentences.en: I tell my mother to sit down next to me.
sentences.zh: 我叫我母亲坐在我旁边。

sentences.en: What did you play?
sentences.zh: 你弹了什么？

sentences.en: I don't quite remember what I played that time, but I was doing more of a, I was, I wanted to sing to her for some reason because it was such an emotional thing.
sentences.zh: 我不记得那次弹了什么，但我弹得更多的是，我想为她唱歌，因为那是一种非常感人的时刻。

sentences.en: And I, and I, and I was going into like, and I just started to kind of chord this.
sentences.zh: 我开始弹奏和弦。

sentences.en: And she was looking at me like, whoa, when did this transpire?
sentences.zh: 她看着我，心想：哇，这是什么时候发生的？

sentences.en: She, I mean, she had all kinds of questions right away.
sentences.zh: 她立刻问了一连串的问题。

sentences.en: And then I just kind of went nuts and started going crazy just to show her, well, look at this, look at this.
sentences.zh: 然后我就有点疯了，开始疯狂弹奏，只是为了向她展示：看这个，看这个。

sentences.en: And she, she started crying.
sentences.zh: 她开始哭了起来。

sentences.en: She, she didn't really say much.
sentences.zh: 她没说什么。

sentences.en: It was a very quiet drive home.
sentences.zh: 回家的路上非常安静。

sentences.en: As you're telling me this, Derek, I almost have the feeling that you are pulling my leg right now because it seems this is not possible.
sentences.zh: 德里克，当你告诉我这些时，我几乎觉得你在开玩笑，因为这似乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: This is just simply not, it could not have happened.
sentences.zh: 这根本不可能，这不可能发生。

sentences.en: You know, well, if I would have had my way, I'm not sure if I would have ended up a piano player.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我有选择的话，我不确定自己是否会成为一名钢琴家。

sentences.en: I kind of wanted to be a baseball player or work in the fighting business.
sentences.zh: 我本来想成为一名棒球运动员，或者从事格斗行业。

sentences.en: So, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以，我不知道。

sentences.en: I, I, and, and you know what?
sentences.zh: 我，而且，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I invite skepticism because I think when something so beautiful and profound happens, we have to, we have to question.
sentences.zh: 我欢迎质疑，因为我认为当如此美丽而深刻的事情发生时，我们必须提出质疑。

sentences.en: At what stage did you stop questioning that you had a skill?
sentences.zh: 你在哪个阶段停止质疑自己拥有这项技能的？

sentences.en: I'm assuming that you were skeptical as well.
sentences.zh: 我假设你当时也很怀疑。

sentences.en: I mean, you told me that when you went home the first night, you were afraid that it was going to be a one day skill and it was going to be gone by the next morning.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你告诉我第一天晚上回家时，你很担心这只是一天的技能，第二天早上就会消失。

sentences.en: At what point did you stop questioning it and say, this is actually a new skill that I have?
sentences.zh: 你在什么时候停止了质疑，并说：这确实是我拥有的新技能？

sentences.en: You know, I, I think you kind of grow into that, getting comfortable with accepting what's transpired in your life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想你是慢慢适应了这一点，开始坦然接受生活中发生的一切。

sentences.en: I definitely didn't want it to go away.
sentences.zh: 我绝对不想让它消失。

sentences.en: In the first year or two, it was a little, you know, like I would wake up thinking, I need to get to a piano.
sentences.zh: 头一两年，有点像……你知道，我醒来时会想，我得去弹钢琴。

sentences.en: I need to make sure it's still here.
sentences.zh: 我得确认它还在。

sentences.en: And then as time went on, I started to understand that, well, the doctors tell me it can go away as fast as it came.
sentences.zh: 后来随着时间推移，我开始明白，嗯，医生告诉我，它来得快，去得也可能很快。

sentences.en: And acquired musical savant syndrome, that means you've acquired a gift.
sentences.zh: 而获得性学者综合征，意味着你获得了一份天赋。

sentences.en: And I got to that point where I, I just accepted the fact that I'm going to enjoy every, every second of this.
sentences.zh: 我到了那个地步，我只是接受了这样一个事实：我要享受这一切的每一秒。

sentences.en: Because if I wake up tomorrow and it's gone, I want to be able to say that I, I did the best I could to display it to a society looking in at my life and say,
sentences.zh: 因为如果明天醒来它消失了，我希望能够说，我尽了最大努力向审视我生活的人们展示它，并说，

sentences.en: I've been inspired by this or the human potential is amazing.
sentences.zh: 我从中受到了启发，或者人类的潜能是惊人的。

sentences.en: Or the brain is just a magnificent, you know, organ that we don't know anything about.
sentences.zh: 或者大脑只是一个宏伟的、你知道的、我们一无所知的器官。

sentences.en: And I think it became that comfort knowing that I'm going to enjoy it every single second.
sentences.zh: 我认为这变成了一种安慰，因为我知道我会享受它的每一秒。

sentences.en: And if it stays beautiful, if it goes away, then I guess I'll go get a job.
sentences.zh: 如果它保持美好，如果它消失了，那我想我得去找份工作。

sentences.en: Have you spoken to a neurologist who is skeptical about what's happening to you?
sentences.zh: 你有没有咨询过对你身上发生的事情持怀疑态度的神经科医生？

sentences.en: I think they're all skeptical the moment they walk in the door.
sentences.zh: 我想他们走进门的那一刻都是怀疑的。

sentences.en: I mean, I feel skeptical.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我自己也感到怀疑。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: I know that.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I know that you're a nice guy and you seem like a trustworthy person.
sentences.zh: 我知道你是个好人，看起来是个值得信赖的人。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: I expect you to be.
sentences.zh: 我希望你是。

sentences.en: But I have the feeling that you're just, this is just one big giant prank.
sentences.zh: 但我有一种感觉，你只是……这只是一个巨大的恶作剧。

sentences.en: Well, that's because I, I'm still, I, I'm articulate and I, and I still have most of my marbles.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是因为我……我仍然……我……我表达清晰，而且我……我大部分理智还在。

sentences.en: So I can, I can display the story in a different way than let's say the guy that hit his head and woke up a piano player, but he's not all here.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以……我可以以一种不同于那种撞了头醒来就成了钢琴家，但神志不清的人的方式来讲述这个故事。

sentences.en: If I asked you to play Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star for me, could you try that?
sentences.zh: 如果我让你为我弹奏《一闪一闪小星星》，你能试试吗？

sentences.en: I don't think I can play it.
sentences.zh: 我想我弹不出来。

sentences.en: I tried to do Happy Birthday for a person the other day and I couldn't figure it out.
sentences.zh: 前几天我试着给一个人弹《生日快乐歌》，但我没搞明白。

sentences.en: Um, oh, answer's no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，哦，答案是不行。

sentences.en: Start with C.
sentences.zh: 从C音开始。

sentences.en: Is that this one right here?
sentences.zh: 是这一个吗？

sentences.en: Wait.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: Where was that first note then?
sentences.zh: 那第一个音在哪里？

sentences.en: Wait.
sentences.zh: 等等。

sentences.en: Where, oh.
sentences.zh: 在哪里，哦。

sentences.en: So it's all up and down.
sentences.zh: 所以它是忽高忽低的。

sentences.en: Gosh darn it.
sentences.zh: 该死。

sentences.en: I see, I see, I can see it now.
sentences.zh: 我明白了，我明白了，我现在能看出来了。

sentences.en: It's kind of in there.
sentences.zh: 它就在里面。

sentences.en: Thanks for the first note though.
sentences.zh: 不过还是谢谢你给的第一个音。

sentences.en: But it's sort of an interesting thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 但这确实是一件有趣的事，不是吗？

sentences.en: Which is like, you, you, you don't go up, you don't see someone who says, you know, I, I can throw a fastball at, I don't know, 140 miles an hour,
sentences.zh: 就像，你……你……你不会去……你不会看到有人说，你知道，我……我能投出时速……我不知道，140英里的快球，

sentences.en: but I don't know how to reach out and shake your hand.
sentences.zh: 但我不知道怎么伸手去和你握手。

sentences.en: And to me, you're displaying musical ability at one end of the spectrum, whereas playing Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, I can do that.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，你在光谱的一端展示了音乐天赋，而弹奏《一闪一闪小星星》，我能做到。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you, you find it hard and I find it just really difficult to understand how you can be so good at the extreme end.
sentences.zh: 而你觉得很难，我真的很难理解你怎么能在极端的一端表现得如此出色。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Without knowing the basics.
sentences.zh: 却不懂基础知识。

sentences.en: I'm right there with you.
sentences.zh: 我和你有同感。

sentences.en: I'm, I'm, I'm on your side.
sentences.zh: 我……我……我站在你这边。

sentences.en: I, I'm fascinated with that too.
sentences.zh: 我……我也对此着迷。

sentences.en: Does it disturb you?
sentences.zh: 这让你感到困扰吗？

sentences.en: Does it worry you that you have this ability?
sentences.zh: 拥有这种能力让你担心吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm a Christian kid, so I think, I think this is where God wants me.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我是个基督徒孩子，所以我认为，我认为这就是上帝希望我所在的地方。

sentences.en: I think this has already been penned out, my story.
sentences.zh: 我认为我的故事早已注定。

sentences.en: I, I, I, how else, I mean, I have to live with this every day.
sentences.zh: 我……我……我，还能怎样，我是说，我每天都得带着这个生活。

sentences.en: So if I sit and beat my own mind up about, is this nature versus nurture and nature and all this nonsense.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我坐在这里，为这是先天还是后天，以及所有这些废话而折磨自己的大脑。

sentences.en: But, I mean, I've talked to the best doctors, the smartest doctors on this planet.
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说，我和这个星球上最好的医生、最聪明的医生谈过。

sentences.en: And they all got a different little input and they all got something different to say about it.
sentences.zh: 他们每个人都有不同的看法，对这件事都有不同的说法。

sentences.en: Most all of them are skeptic when I walk in.
sentences.zh: 我走进去时，他们几乎所有人都是怀疑的。

sentences.en: And most all of them when I walk out are right here with me.
sentences.zh: 而当我走出来时，他们几乎所有人都和我站在了一起。

sentences.en: Have any of them suggested treatments?
sentences.zh: 他们中有人建议过治疗方案吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 有。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 有。

sentences.en: They, um, Dr. Reeves at the, at the Mayo Clinic, when I was filming with the Discovery Channel, he was fascinated with this as well.
sentences.zh: 他们，嗯，梅奥诊所的里夫斯医生，我在拍摄探索频道节目时，他也对此非常着迷。

sentences.en: And he said, the best way for him to explain it is like a rollercoaster.
sentences.zh: 他说，他解释这件事最好的方式就像过山车。

sentences.en: If you get on a rollercoaster that doesn't stop, sooner or later it's going to get tiring.
sentences.zh: 如果你坐上一辆不停的过山车，迟早会感到疲惫。

sentences.en: So maybe we suggest slowing down the stimulant, the overstimulated brain.
sentences.zh: 所以也许我们建议减缓这种刺激，这种过度刺激的大脑。

sentences.en: You're firing these neurons at a pace that's unheard of.
sentences.zh: 你以一种闻所未闻的速度激发这些神经元。

sentences.en: So, let's try some seizure medication to shut those down, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们尝试一些抗癫痫药物来抑制它们，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't know, understand how it works, but I do know it slows down the firing of the neurons.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，不明白它是如何运作的，但我确实知道它减缓了神经元的激发。

sentences.en: Oh, why, why would I want to take synthetic drugs and, and mask something possibly that I'm enjoying to the point where I don't want, I don't want it to slow down and go away.
sentences.zh: 哦，为什么，我为什么要服用合成药物，去掩盖我可能正在享受的东西，以至于我不想，我不想让它减慢并消失。

sentences.en: Okay, I'll take the hyperness and the ADHD and the OCD and all that garbage that comes with this maybe.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我接受这种亢奋、多动症、强迫症以及随之而来的所有垃圾。

sentences.en: What if it has a consequence where you are burning your brain at a level that is not healthy for you?
sentences.zh: 如果它有一个后果，就是你在以一种对你不健康的方式燃烧你的大脑呢？

sentences.en: I mean, so for example, let's say...
sentences.zh: 我是说，举个例子，假设……

sentences.en: Then I guess I go down on fire, baby.
sentences.zh: 那我想我就在火中倒下吧，宝贝。

sentences.en: And that's how the story ends, and I'm good with that.
sentences.zh: 故事就是这样结束的，我对此没意见。

sentences.en: You're still the guy who would die for the football over the swimming pool.
sentences.zh: 你依然是那个为了游泳池里的橄榄球而不顾一切的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Of course, Derek Amado isn't the only person with Acquired Savant Syndrome.
sentences.zh: 当然，德里克·阿马多并不是唯一患有获得性学者综合征的人。

sentences.en: Others have experienced the profound changes that come with this condition.
sentences.zh: 其他人也经历过这种状况带来的深刻变化。

sentences.en: They are so motivated.
sentences.zh: 他们非常有动力。

sentences.en: They are in love with what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 他们热爱自己所做的事情。

sentences.en: It's almost like an extension of who they are.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是他们自身的一种延伸。

sentences.en: Also, I'm going to challenge Derek to play the studio wall.
sentences.zh: 另外，我要挑战德里克去弹奏演播室的墙壁。

sentences.en: I see on this wall, I see these squares.
sentences.zh: 我在这面墙上看到了这些方块。

sentences.en: Some of them have different depths, so the full squares almost feel like a whole note to me.
sentences.zh: 其中一些有不同的深度，所以完整的方块对我来说几乎感觉像是一个全音符。

sentences.en: Keep listening.
sentences.zh: 继续听。

sentences.en: It'll make more sense soon.
sentences.zh: 很快就会更有意义了。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham, and you're listening to Hidden Brain from NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆，你正在收听的是NPR的《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This week on the show, we're looking at the specific moments people lose something big
sentences.zh: 本周节目中，我们关注人们失去重要事物的那一刻，

sentences.en: and how that change can point them in new directions.
sentences.zh: 以及这种变化如何将他们引向新的方向。

sentences.en: Before the break, Derek Amado told us the story of how he became a musician after a head injury.
sentences.zh: 休息前，德里克·阿马多告诉我们他在头部受伤后如何成为一名音乐家的故事。

sentences.en: Before the accident, he couldn't play the piano.
sentences.zh: 事故发生前，他不会弹钢琴。

sentences.en: But after, his musical talent was just undeniable.
sentences.zh: 但事故发生后，他的音乐天赋是不可否认的。

sentences.en: If this is the first time you're hearing our show, I have a confession to make.
sentences.zh: 如果这是你第一次收听我们的节目，我得坦白一件事。

sentences.en: I'm a card-carrying rationaliSt.
sentences.zh: 我是一个彻头彻尾的理性主义者。

sentences.en: When surprising things happen, I don't call them miracles.
sentences.zh: 当令人惊讶的事情发生时，我不会称它们为奇迹。

sentences.en: I look for explanations.
sentences.zh: 我会寻找解释。

sentences.en: Derek's very charming.
sentences.zh: 德里克非常有魅力。

sentences.en: His story is amazing.
sentences.zh: 他的故事令人惊叹。

sentences.en: But I found myself asking over and over how something like this could happen.
sentences.zh: 但我发现自己一遍又一遍地问，这种事怎么可能发生。

sentences.en: That's when I came by a couple of researchers who've spent years studying people who've suddenly
sentences.zh: 那时我遇到了一些研究人员，他们花了多年时间研究那些突然

sentences.en: acquired savant-like gifts.
sentences.zh: 获得学者般天赋的人。

sentences.en: Daryl Treffert is a psychiatrist in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 达里尔·特雷弗特是威斯康星州的一名精神科医生。

sentences.en: He studied Derek.
sentences.zh: 他研究过德里克。

sentences.en: And I must say that in his case, I was as startled as you about the fact that he went to the piano
sentences.zh: 我必须说，在他的案例中，我和你一样惊讶，因为他走到钢琴前，

sentences.en: and knew where to place his fingers and so forth.
sentences.zh: 就知道把手指放在哪里等等。

sentences.en: The reason that I'm inclined to accept that is because I've seen that in some of these other cases.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于接受这一点的原因是，我在其他一些案例中也见过这种情况。

sentences.en: Although probably not quite as abrupt as he, and to me at least, that having seen a lot of savants,
sentences.zh: 虽然可能不像他那样突然，而且至少对我来说，在见过很多学者之后，

sentences.en: when I see some of these acquired savant cases, it is really quite jarring.
sentences.zh: 当我看到这些获得性学者案例时，确实非常令人震惊。

sentences.en: I don't know if you remember what Derek said about his injury.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你是否记得德里克关于他受伤的描述。

sentences.en: He leaped across the swimming pool for the football, and when he came down hard,
sentences.zh: 他为了接橄榄球跳过游泳池，当他重重落下时，

sentences.en: he heard what sounded like an explosion.
sentences.zh: 他听到了听起来像爆炸的声音。

sentences.en: And I miscalculated the depth, obviously, and I hit the upper left side of my face.
sentences.zh: 显然我误判了深度，我的脸左上侧撞到了。

sentences.en: The left side of his face.
sentences.zh: 他脸的左侧。

sentences.en: That's an important clue.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重要的线索。

sentences.en: In general, in savant syndrome itself, whether congenital or acquired,
sentences.zh: 总的来说，在学者综合征本身中，无论是先天的还是后天的，

sentences.en: there tends to be a more left brain injury with right brain compensation.
sentences.zh: 往往是左脑损伤伴随右脑补偿。

sentences.en: And the right brain areas of ability that seem to emerge have to do with art, music, and mathematics, actually.
sentences.zh: 而出现的右脑能力区域实际上与艺术、音乐和数学有关。

sentences.en: Art, music, and math.
sentences.zh: 艺术、音乐和数学。

sentences.en: All skills that involve pattern recognition.
sentences.zh: 所有涉及模式识别的技能。

sentences.en: At the University of Pennsylvania, cognitive psychologist Scott Barry Kaufman said,
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚大学，认知心理学家斯科特·巴里·考夫曼说，

sentences.en: think about it.
sentences.zh: 想一想。

sentences.en: These are the skills you might imagine are built into the architecture of the brain.
sentences.zh: 这些是你可能会想象内置在大脑结构中的技能。

sentences.en: In other words, we might come hardwired for certain kinds of activities.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，我们可能天生就具备了某些活动的硬件。

sentences.en: This is the insight that helped me see that Derek might not be pulling a prank.
sentences.zh: 正是这种洞察力让我明白德里克可能不是在搞恶作剧。

sentences.en: Most of us, in fact, effortlessly learn things.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们大多数人都是毫不费力地学习东西的。

sentences.en: Just like Derek says he never took classes to learn piano,
sentences.zh: 就像德里克说他从未上过钢琴课一样，

sentences.en: you probably didn't take formal lessons to learn your first language.
sentences.zh: 你可能也没有上过正式课程来学习你的第一语言。

sentences.en: The truth is that a lot of things we learn in life were not done deliberately.
sentences.zh: 事实是，我们在生活中学习的很多东西都不是刻意为之的。

sentences.en: When we were very young, in the ages of two and four,
sentences.zh: 当我们很小的时候，在两到四岁之间，

sentences.en: we learned a huge amount of new words
sentences.zh: 我们学习了大量的生词，

sentences.en: and learned the grammatical structure of our language automatically.
sentences.zh: 并自动掌握了我们语言的语法结构。

sentences.en: We didn't sit down when we were two years old and say,
sentences.zh: 我们两岁时并没有坐下来对自己说，

sentences.en: right, I'm going to learn all the grammatical syntax and what it all means.
sentences.zh: 好，我要学习所有的语法句法以及它们的意思。

sentences.en: And so we have these structures that help us learn.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拥有这些帮助我们学习的结构。

sentences.en: If you look at it this way, most people have skills that might seem savant-like
sentences.zh: 如果你这样看，大多数人拥有的技能在来自另一个星球的访客看来，

sentences.en: to a visitor from another planet.
sentences.zh: 可能看起来像学者一样。

sentences.en: We learn these skills effortlessly.
sentences.zh: 我们毫不费力地学习这些技能。

sentences.en: In fact, it doesn't even feel like learning.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这甚至感觉不像是在学习。

sentences.en: It feels like fun.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是在玩。

sentences.en: What makes savants unique, in other words,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，是什么让学者变得独特，

sentences.en: is not that their brains do amazing things.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为他们的大脑做了惊人的事情。

sentences.en: All brains do amazing things.
sentences.zh: 所有的大脑都会做惊人的事情。

sentences.en: What's different is that they're demonstrating effortless learning
sentences.zh: 不同之处在于，他们展示了毫不费力的学习，

sentences.en: in domains that usually call for sustained effort.
sentences.zh: 而在通常需要持续努力的领域。

sentences.en: Now, I'm not going to tell you you should go out and bang your head
sentences.zh: 现在，我不是要告诉你，你应该去撞击你的头，

sentences.en: against the floor of a swimming pool to learn to play the piano.
sentences.zh: 撞向游泳池的底部来学习弹钢琴。

sentences.en: The vast majority of concussions don't produce an inner genius.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数脑震荡并不会让人变成天才。

sentences.en: They have terrible outcomes.
sentences.zh: 它们往往会带来可怕的后果。

sentences.en: But Derek's story does suggest, even to this card-carrying rationalist,
sentences.zh: 但德瑞克的故事确实向我——即便是我这种坚定的理性主义者——表明，

sentences.en: that we have worlds within us, gifts, that we do not realize that we possess.
sentences.zh: 我们内心深处蕴藏着我们自己都未曾察觉的世界和天赋。

sentences.en: When I look at these savants, what I see at the core
sentences.zh: 当我观察这些学者症候群患者时，我所看到的内核，

sentences.en: that I think offers a lot of inspiration to humanity
sentences.zh: 我认为能给人类带来很多启发的地方，

sentences.en: is that they are so motivated.
sentences.zh: 在于他们有着极强的动力。

sentences.en: They are in love with what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 他们热爱自己所做的事情。

sentences.en: It's almost like an extension of who they are.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是他们自身的一种延伸。

sentences.en: To me, that offers a lot of hope or inspires me
sentences.zh: 对我而言，这带来了很多希望，或者说启发了我，

sentences.en: that perhaps all of us can find that vehicle
sentences.zh: 也许我们每个人都能找到那个载体，

sentences.en: that really allows us to sing.
sentences.zh: 那个真正能让我们引吭高歌的载体。

sentences.en: As Derek was playing the piano in NPR Studio One,
sentences.zh: 当德瑞克在 NPR 一号演播室弹奏钢琴时，

sentences.en: I noticed there was a wall behind him.
sentences.zh: 我注意到他身后有一面墙。

sentences.en: It had soundproofing, hollow wooden cubes, each of a different depth.
sentences.zh: 那上面有隔音用的空心木块，每个木块的深度各不相同。

sentences.en: Derek had told me that when he plays,
sentences.zh: 德瑞克曾告诉我，当他弹奏时，

sentences.en: he sees squares floating by him.
sentences.zh: 他能看到一个个方块在他面前飘过。

sentences.en: So I asked him to turn around, look at the wall,
sentences.zh: 所以我让他转过身，看着那面墙，

sentences.en: and tell me what he saw.
sentences.zh: 告诉我他看到了什么。

sentences.en: I see on this wall, I see these squares.
sentences.zh: 我在这面墙上看到了这些方块。

sentences.en: Some of them have different depths,
sentences.zh: 它们有的深度不同，

sentences.en: so the full squares almost feel like a whole note to me.
sentences.zh: 所以那些完整的方块对我来说几乎就像是一个全音符。

sentences.en: I asked Derek to play the wall for me.
sentences.zh: 我让德瑞克为我弹奏这面墙。

sentences.en: I see low notes because all the depth.
sentences.zh: 我看到了低音，因为它们有深度。

sentences.en: You see the dark ones that are filled in all the way?
sentences.zh: 你看到那些完全填满的深色方块了吗？

sentences.en: They stand out, so I see low notes like...
sentences.zh: 它们很突出，所以我看到了像这样的低音……

sentences.en: Now I'm in the middle boxes.
sentences.zh: 现在我弹到中间的方块了。

sentences.en: See where I'm at now in those middle boxes?
sentences.zh: 看到我现在弹到中间那些方块的位置了吗？

sentences.en: So those are...
sentences.zh: 所以那些是……

sentences.en: And that's a whole different...
sentences.zh: 那又是完全不同的……

sentences.en: Now we're getting into a whole different thing.
sentences.zh: 现在我们进入了一个完全不同的领域。

sentences.en: Now I'm getting excited.
sentences.zh: 我现在开始兴奋了。

sentences.en: Got any more walls to look at?
sentences.zh: 还有别的墙可以看吗？

sentences.en: So you were just playing the wall?
sentences.zh: 所以你刚才是在弹奏那面墙？

sentences.en: That's what you were playing?
sentences.zh: 你刚才弹的就是那个？

sentences.en: I was playing what I...
sentences.zh: 我弹奏的是我……

sentences.en: So I started here.
sentences.zh: 我是从这里开始的。

sentences.en: Okay, so imagine that's the music bar.
sentences.zh: 好的，想象一下那就是乐谱的音轨。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I played the top one.
sentences.zh: 所以我弹了最上面那一行。

sentences.en: I'll do it again.
sentences.zh: 我再弹一遍。

sentences.en: I'll do it precisely exactly like I saw it.
sentences.zh: 我会完全按照我看到的样子精准地弹出来。

sentences.en: And then it changes to this bar.
sentences.zh: 然后它变成了这一行。

sentences.en: We've moved down now,
sentences.zh: 我们现在移到了下面，

sentences.en: and now we're going to move down to the next bar of music.
sentences.zh: 现在我们要移到下一行乐谱。

sentences.en: And I see...
sentences.zh: 我看到……

sentences.en: Then we'll go back up to the top.
sentences.zh: 然后我们再回到最上面。

sentences.en: And then we can make it jazz.
sentences.zh: 接着我们可以把它变成爵士乐。

sentences.en: And that's...
sentences.zh: 而那……

sentences.en: And I mean, it just goes on and on and on and on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它就这样没完没了地持续下去。

sentences.en: And these walls could be dangerous
sentences.zh: 这些墙可能会很危险，

sentences.en: because I wouldn't want to sleep at all
sentences.zh: 因为如果我家有这样的墙，

sentences.en: if I had walls like this at my house.
sentences.zh: 我根本就不想睡觉了。

sentences.en: Are you telling me that you have never played
sentences.zh: 你是说你从来没有弹过

sentences.en: the piece of music you just played for me
sentences.zh: 你刚才为我弹奏的那段音乐吗？

sentences.en: in your life before?
sentences.zh: 你以前从未弹过？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: And this third row might even be
sentences.zh: 而且这第三行甚至可能

sentences.en: a whole different composition.
sentences.zh: 是完全不同的另一首曲子。

sentences.en: That's what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 我就是这个意思。

sentences.en: The depths of those blocks,
sentences.zh: 那些方块的深度，

sentences.en: those middle rows and those circles in the middle,
sentences.zh: 中间的那些行和中间的那些圆圈，

sentences.en: that's what these are to me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说就是这些东西。

sentences.en: Those are rolling patterns to me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那些是流动的旋律模式。

sentences.en: And then those chunky ones on the top,
sentences.zh: 还有上面那些厚实的方块，

sentences.en: that's where I see that.
sentences.zh: 那就是我看到的地方。

sentences.en: And it just changes like that suddenly.
sentences.zh: 它就这样突然改变了。

sentences.en: And then I moved out of the next one,
sentences.zh: 然后我移到了下一个，

sentences.en: and it's a whole different flow.
sentences.zh: 那是完全不同的节奏流。

sentences.zh: 以上是德瑞克·阿马托在 NPR 一号演播室弹奏墙壁的片段。
